story: Alaska draws the third-largest E-Rate check in the nation, and the FCC (comments due October 13th) is asking whether to limit or sunset the program and what connectivity schools need for AI tools.

claims.claim: The FCC's E-Rate notice in the Federal Register sets October 13th, 2026 as the deadline for comments.
claims.verbatim: Comments are due on or before October 13, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590, 91 FR 52626)
claims.notes: Docket Nos. 26-133, 13-184, 21-93, 21-455, FCC 26-41. Corroborated by FCC Public Notice DA 26-865 (C16). The fetch tool reported that the word Alaska appears nowhere in the full Federal Register text; that is a note only, not a claim, because absence was reported by the fetch summarizer rather than by an independent text search.

claims.claim: Reply comments on the FCC's E-Rate notice are due November 12th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: reply comments are due on or before November 12, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590, 91 FR 52626)
claims.notes: Corroborated by DA 26-865 (C16).

claims.claim: The FCC asks in its E-Rate notice whether the E-Rate program should be limited or sunset to reflect today's extensive connectivity rates.
claims.verbatim: Should the E-Rate program be limited or sunset to reflect today's extensive connectivity rates?
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590, 91 FR 52626)
claims.notes: It is a question put out for comment, not a proposal or decision. Frame as 'asks whether'.

claims.claim: The notice cites an executive order on artificial intelligence whose goal is to equip educators to use AI in their classrooms to improve educational outcomes.
claims.verbatim: an executive order addressing Artificial Intelligence (AI) identifies as a goal to 'invest in our educators and equip them with the tools and knowledge to not only train students about AI, but also to utilize AI in their classrooms to improve educational outcomes.'
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590, 91 FR 52626)
claims.notes: Verbatim is 41 words including the lead-in; trim to the goal clause if it must be shown. Inner quotation marks are single quotes on the page. The fetch tool reported this as the sentence immediately preceding the AI connectivity question (C05).

claims.claim: The FCC asks what level of connectivity schools and libraries need to use AI-enabled educational tools or other emerging technologies effectively.
claims.verbatim: What level of connectivity do schools and libraries need to utilize AI-enabled educational tools or other emerging technologies effectively?
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590, 91 FR 52626)
claims.notes: A question for comment.

claims.claim: The FCC asks whether the discount rate for rural schools and libraries should be higher than the discount rate for urban schools and libraries.
claims.verbatim: Should the discount rate for rural schools and libraries be higher than the discount rate for urban schools and libraries?
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590, 91 FR 52626)
claims.notes: A question for comment. Relevant to Alaska by inference only, since the notice never names the state.

claims.claim: The FCC notice raises the concern of a disproportionate share of E-Rate funding flowing to large, well-resourced school districts with substantial local tax bases.
claims.verbatim: a disproportionate share of funding flow to large, well-resourced school districts with substantial local tax bases
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590, 91 FR 52626)
claims.notes: needs_softening true. Only the fragment was returned by the fetch tool, so whether it is posed as a question or as an observation is not confirmed. Write 'raises the concern' or 'asks whether', not 'finds'.

claims.claim: E-Rate discounts range from 20% to 90%, according to the FCC notice.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590, 91 FR 52626)
claims.notes: Same range is used by AASB (C33), which frames it as costs districts would absorb.

claims.claim: Applicants requested $1.806 billion for Category 1 services (connections to schools) in funding year 2025.
claims.verbatim: applicants requesting $1.806 billion in funding year 2025 for category one services (i.e., connections to schools)
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590, 91 FR 52626)
claims.notes: Requests, not commitments. Do not compare with USAC funded commitment totals (C17 to C21), which are a different measure.

claims.claim: Applicants requested $1.418 billion for Category 2 services in funding year 2025.
claims.verbatim: $1.418 billion in funding year 2025 for category two services
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590, 91 FR 52626)
claims.notes: Requests, not commitments.

claims.claim: The FCC adopted its E-Rate notice (FCC 26-41) on June 25th, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission (FCC 26-41)
claims.notes: The same line shows release on June 26th, 2026.

claims.claim: The FCC asks whether E-Rate support should be limited to rural areas or to areas served by a single provider.
claims.value: rural areas or a single provider
claims.verbatim: should E-Rate support be limited to rural areas or to areas served by a single provider?
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission (FCC 26-41)
claims.notes: Paragraph 26, framed as 'support should be limited to areas where applicants face the highest costs'. Same paragraph states current rules raise the rural discount by five to ten percentage points for applicants below 80 percent. Question for comment only.

claims.claim: The FCC asks whether E-Rate funding should be conditioned on the imposition of screen time limits in schools and libraries.
claims.verbatim: whether E-Rate funding should be conditioned on the imposition of screen time limits in schools and libraries
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission (FCC 26-41)
claims.notes: Paragraph 30. Question for comment only.

claims.claim: The FCC asks whether schools should be required, as a condition of E-Rate support, to give parents a meaningful opportunity to opt their children out of screen-based instruction.
claims.verbatim: should require, as a condition of receiving E-Rate support, that participating schools provide parents with a meaningful opportunity to opt their children out of screen-based instruction
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission (FCC 26-41)
claims.notes: Paragraph 31. Question for comment only. Verbatim is 33 words.

claims.claim: An FCC Public Notice released August 17th, 2026 sets October 13th as the comment deadline and November 12th as the reply deadline.
claims.verbatim: Comments Due: October 13, 2026 Reply Comments Due: November 12, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission (Public Notice DA 26-865)
claims.notes: Independent corroboration of C01 and C02. Docket Nos. 26-133, 13-184, 21-93, 21-455. The notice text returned by the fetch tool does not state the electronic filing system, so filing method (ECFS) is NOT claimed.

claims.claim: Alaska schools and libraries had $195.2 million in funded E-Rate commitments for funding year 2025.
claims.source_outlet: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC Open Data, E-Rate request dataset)
claims.notes: Sum of funding_commitment_request for Alaska FRNs with status Funded, 388 requests. Date is the fetch date since USAC data is live and can change. The same fetch returned FY2024 221,389,113.58 and FY2026 175,676,180.60 (partial year).

claims.claim: Alaska schools and libraries had $93.0 million in funded E-Rate commitments for funding year 2017.
claims.source_outlet: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC Open Data, E-Rate request dataset)
claims.notes: 328 requests. FY2025 (C16) is about 2.1 times this figure in nominal dollars.

claims.claim: Alaska ranked third among states in funded E-Rate commitments for funding year 2025, behind California and Texas.
claims.source_outlet: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC Open Data, E-Rate request dataset)
claims.notes: Query ordered by total descending. Top five returned were CA 380.3M, TX 233.6M, AK 195.2M, NY 181.2M, FL 100.6M. Rank is by funded commitment dollars, not per capita. Verbatim is separated by JSON line breaks on the page.

claims.claim: National funded E-Rate commitments for funding year 2025 total $2.69 billion.
claims.source_outlet: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC Open Data, E-Rate request dataset)
claims.notes: 52,191 funded requests nationally. Denominator for C20.

claims.claim: Alaska's funded E-Rate commitments for funding year 2025 are about 7.3 percent of the national total.
claims.source_outlet: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC Open Data, E-Rate request dataset)
claims.notes: Derived. 195,225,505.86 / 2,687,663,041.80 = 0.07264, so 7.3 percent. Numerator is from the Alaska by year query (C16), denominator from this national query. Verbatim joins two JSON values from two fetches.

claims.claim: Alaska's population estimate for July 1st, 2025 is 737,270.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Census Bureau (QuickFacts, Vintage 2025)
claims.notes: Direct WebFetch of census.gov returned 403 (as did the quickfacts/AK page). Figure was read through the r.jina.ai reader rendering of the same census.gov URL. Date is the estimate reference date. Confidence held below 0.9 for that reason; a reader can confirm at the URL.

claims.claim: The United States population estimate for July 1st, 2025 is 341,784,857.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Census Bureau (QuickFacts, Vintage 2025)
claims.notes: Same access caveat as C21.

claims.claim: Alaska holds about 0.2 percent of the U.S. population, against about 7.3 percent of funding year 2025 funded E-Rate commitments.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Census Bureau (QuickFacts, Vintage 2025)
claims.notes: Derived. 737,270 / 341,784,857 = 0.002157, so 0.2 percent. The 7.3 percent half rests on C20. Ratio of shares is roughly 34 to 1. Same access caveat as C21.

claims.claim: Lower Kuskokwim School District had $91.0 million in funded E-Rate commitments for funding year 2025, the most of any Alaska applicant.
claims.source_outlet: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC Open Data, E-Rate request dataset)
claims.notes: Five requests. DISCREPANCY NOT RESOLVED. The Anchorage Daily News reports Lower Kuskokwim received $96.5 million in E-Rate funding in the 2025 calendar year, which differs from USAC funded FRN commitments for funding year 2025. Likely different scope or timing. Cite each to its own source and do not blend them.

claims.claim: Lower Kuskokwim School District accounts for about 46.6 percent of Alaska's funding year 2025 funded E-Rate commitments.
claims.source_outlet: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC Open Data, E-Rate request dataset)
claims.notes: Derived. 91,025,198.22 / 195,225,505.86 = 0.46623, so 46.6 percent. Denominator from C16.

claims.claim: The top three Alaska applicants for funding year 2025 total about $128.3 million in funded E-Rate commitments, which is 65.7 percent of the state total.
claims.source_outlet: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC Open Data, E-Rate request dataset)
claims.notes: Derived. 91,025,198.22 + 25,554,156.01 + 11,710,186.13 = 128,289,540.36; divided by 195,225,505.86 = 0.65715, so 65.7 percent. Districts are Lower Kuskokwim, Bering Strait and Northwest Arctic Borough.

claims.claim: Alaska's 45 school districts hold $192.4 million, or 98.6 percent, of the state's funding year 2025 funded E-Rate commitments.
claims.source_outlet: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC Open Data, E-Rate request dataset)
claims.notes: Derived share. 192,419,347.75 / 195,225,505.86 = 0.98563. The five entity types sum exactly to 195,225,505.86 (checked). Libraries (61 orgs) hold 1,460,264.36; consortia (12) 1,070,813.37; library systems (5) 100,655.58; individual schools (7) 174,424.80.

claims.claim: Lower Yukon School District's largest internet access line in funding year 2023 was $9,229,248 with GCI Communication Corp.
claims.source_outlet: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC Open Data, E-Rate request dataset)
claims.notes: The identical $9,229,248 GCI line also appears in funding year 2022. The ADN reports a different figure for the same district (about $6.25 million the year before the switch, see C31), so use each figure only with its own attribution.

claims.claim: Lower Yukon School District's largest internet access line in funding year 2024 was $373,345 with Sateo Inc dba Microcom.
claims.source_outlet: Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC Open Data, E-Rate request dataset)
claims.notes: Value is 373,345.20 in the data. Funding year 2025 Sateo line is 313,070.40. USAC data does not say the district moved to Starlink; that comes from the ADN (C31). Calling the provider switch a cause of the drop is the ADN's framing, not USAC's.

claims.claim: Lower Yukon School District moved to Starlink in 2024 and its E-Rate internet subsidy dropped from about $6.25 million to about $600,000, according to the Anchorage Daily News.
claims.verbatim: Lower Yukon received about $6.25 million through E-Rate for internet. In 2024, when they switched to Starlink, that subsidy amount dropped to about $600,000.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Alaska Journal of Commerce), Mari Kanagy
claims.notes: needs_softening true. Attribute to ADN. Figures differ from USAC FRN values (C28, C29), so do not present as one series. Byline date on the page read August 9th, 2026 while the URL path is 2026/08/10; both stated. Quote was returned through the fetch tool summarizer, so treat exact wording as slightly less certain.

claims.claim: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said the agency should consider reducing the E-Rate program's scope, according to the Anchorage Daily News.
claims.verbatim: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said the agency should consider reducing the program's scope
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Alaska Journal of Commerce), Mari Kanagy
claims.notes: needs_softening true. The article sentence continues after a dash with 'or cutting it altogether'; that half is omitted here to avoid the dash and is unverified as an exact string. This is a paraphrase by ADN, not a Carr quote.

claims.claim: Tiffany Jackson of the Association of Alaska School Boards said the E-Rate program is a lifeline to opportunity for Alaska's students.
claims.verbatim: The E-Rate program is a lifeline to opportunity for Alaska's students.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Alaska Journal of Commerce), Mari Kanagy
claims.notes: Named-person quote, returned in that exact wording by the fetch tool. Jackson is also the author of the AASB commentary in C34.

claims.claim: Alaska Gateway School District gets more than $700,000 a year from E-Rate, about 7% of the district's budget, according to Superintendent Patrick Mayer.
claims.verbatim: E-Rate provides more than $700,000 a year for Alaska Gateway, about 7% of the district's budget, Mayer said.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (Chalkbeat), Erica Meltzer
claims.notes: Direct fetch returned 403. Read through the r.jina.ai reader rendering of the same URL, which returned byline Erica Meltzer and date September 28th, 2026. Attribute to Mayer via Chalkbeat/Alaska Beacon.

claims.claim: The Alaska Association of School Boards wrote that districts would face an immediate absorption of full connectivity costs ranging from 20-90% if E-Rate were sunset.
claims.verbatim: Districts would be faced with an immediate absorption of full connectivity costs ranging from 20-90% on broadband, internet, and internal network services.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Association of School Boards (commentary by Tiffany Jackson, 'Preventing a Sunset of the FCC's E-Rate Program')
claims.notes: Advocacy commentary by an interested party, so one-sided framing. needs_softening true, write 'AASB argues'. Range mirrors the FCC discount range in C08.

claims.claim: The full text of the Federal Register notice on the FCC's E-Rate proposal never mentions Alaska.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register via GovInfo (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590)
claims.notes: The zero count is the showrunner's exact string search over the whole downloaded text (210,078 characters). My fetch tool also reported that the word Alaska does not appear anywhere in the document, but it is a summarizer, so that is a corroboration and not an independent exact search. The page header returned was 'Volume 91 Issue 156 (Friday, August 14, 2026)'. The page range 52626 to 52653 was not confirmed by my fetch. Frame the claim as absence of the word, not as a statement about intent. Related to C01, C02.

claims.claim: The FCC's E-Rate notice is filed under WC Docket Nos. 26-133, 13-184, 21-93 and 21-455, and FCC No. 26-41.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register via GovInfo (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590)
claims.notes: Matches DA 26-865 docket list (C15).

claims.claim: The FCC tells electronic filers to submit comments through its ECFS system at fcc.gov/ecfs.
claims.verbatim: Comments may be filed electronically using the internet by accessing the ECFS: https://www.fcc.gov/ecfs/
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register via GovInfo (FCC notice, FR Doc 2026-16590)
claims.notes: The fetch returned the sentence starting at 'Comments may be filed'. The lead-in words 'Electronic Filers:' proposed by the showrunner were not returned as part of the quoted line, so the verbatim omits them. Replaces the ECFS item killed in the first batch.

claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission (FCC 26-41)
claims.notes: Paragraph 26. Same paragraph as the rural or single provider question (C12). Verbatim is 22 words.
